claims_to_fix.statement: SERPINB5 is made almost only by epithelial cells (transit-amplifying and cycling cells in Smillie 2019), with a dominant-lineage share of the transcripts of [gene=SERPINB5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.953]; the epithelial lineage is also dominant in all three other atlases (Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026, GSE282122), so the attribution replicates. The bulk rise is intrinsic: after adjustment for cell proportions the log2FC stays significant at [gene=SERPINB5; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=2.109]; Visium deconvolution also names epithelium as the in-situ source. This is the cleanest cell-and-tissue case in the pool for an epithelial target.

claims_to_fix.statement: CEBPB, the genetics-first candidate, is a broadly expressed transcription factor: neutrophils make a share of its transcripts of [gene=CEBPB; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.698], with macrophages and plasma cells the main Smillie clusters, and the genetically predicted colon dendritic cell is not the dominant source. The bulk increase is mostly composition (partly_composition, retained fraction low), so a CEBPB inhibitor would act on many myeloid cell types at once.

claims.claim: the genetically predicted colon dendritic cell is not the dominant source

claims_to_fix.statement: TUFM, the genetics-first candidate, is a ubiquitous mitochondrial gene (plasma cells and epithelial transit-amplifying cells in Smillie 2019) that does not rise in inflamed bulk tissue: its change is slightly down, with an unadjusted log2FC of [gene=TUFM; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; unadjusted_log2fc=-0.188], opposite to the genetic direction of inhibiting a gene that risk alleles raise, and its cell does not match the predicted blood neutrophil. Single-cell and tissue data do not support it as an inflamed-mucosa target.

claims.claim: its cell does not match the predicted blood neutrophil
